summary: Promoted consent and grant integration into core: added bridge client (AUTH_BRIDGE_URL/timeout/secret), session-protected consent endpoints with grant-first upsert, replaced user_id=0/empty-list placeholders with session-bound ownership-checked handlers, and made get_mcp_grants return only the active grant for immediate revocation.
follow_up: The consent flow is only mounted when AUTH_BRIDGE_URL and AUTH_BRIDGE_SECRET are configured; the grant management API remains the authoritative surface when the bridge is disabled.
The login-continue endpoint is a stub that redirects to the continue URL; a real login form integration would be needed for the full OAuth flow.
important_context: The get_mcp_grants internal API now returns only the active grant (revoked_at IS NULL and not expired), which the mcp-server relies on to resolve at most one grant per (user, client) pair.
The consent flow uses grant-first ordering: the grant is upserted before the bridge decide call, so a bridge failure after grant write leaves a valid grant (safe, user can revoke).
The upsert_grant function uses replace-not-union semantics: re-approving the same (user, client) yields exactly one active grant, preventing accidental broadening.
